featured_videos.title: Keto Flu or Toxic Additives? The Truth About LMNT, Re-Lyte, & Keto Chow
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Tony Hampton - The Metabolic Health Doc
featured_videos.editorial_title: The LMNT Maltodextrin Problem Nobody Talks About
featured_videos.commentary: Dr. Tony Hampton puts three of the most popular electrolyte supplements under the microscope and the comment section turned into a full-on ingredient reckoning. The top comments aren't arguing about which brand is best — they're talking about ditching all of them and making their own for a fraction of the price. Watch it here if you've ever wondered whether your electrolyte packet is quietly working against you. One person ended up in the ER from a potassium miscalculation, which is a useful reminder that "more" is not always the right answer with electrolytes. Worth 20 minutes of your time before you buy your next box.

featured_videos.title: "Low Protein Diet Was Actually The Healthiest"
featured_videos.creator: Kent Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: Protein Minimalism: Bold Claim, Weak Evidence
featured_videos.commentary: The claim that a "low protein diet was actually the healthiest" is the kind of headline that deserves a hard look before you adjust your plate. Kent Carnivore dissects a viral assertion that's circulating in plant-based circles — and the comment section tells you everything you need to know about how carnivore practitioners receive it: one viewer reported doing five sets of thirty pull-ups approaching age 50 after going high-protein in 1994, the same year his vegetarian sister began a lifelong health decline. The actual research picture is more nuanced than either side usually admits: adequate protein intake is associated with preserved lean mass, better satiety signaling, and lower all-cause mortality in middle-aged and older adults. What gets lost in the debate is protein quality and bioavailability — animal proteins supply all essential amino acids in ratios the body can actually use.

featured_videos.title: Finding Love During My Carnivore Weight Loss Journey
featured_videos.creator: Ground Beef Chief
featured_videos.editorial_title: Week 74: He Found Love on Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: Ground Beef Chief has been documenting his carnivore journey for 74 weeks, and this week he introduced his girlfriend Natasha to the internet. The video has 174 comments and basically every single one of them is a variation of "you're absolutely glowing." Nobody planned this part — you start eating meat to lose weight and somewhere along the way you become someone different, and sometimes that someone attracts people. His community didn't just watch it happen, they showed up for it. That's a different kind of before-and-after.

featured_videos.title: This Carnivore System Is a Game Changer
featured_videos.creator: Chris Cooking Nashville
featured_videos.editorial_title: The Carnivore Consistency Problem, Solved Practically
featured_videos.commentary: Most people don't fail carnivore because they lose willpower — they fail because their food is boring and their kitchen habits haven't adapted. Chris Cooking Nashville proposes a systems approach built around a core anchor recipe that makes the diet structurally sustainable rather than relying on motivation alone. From a behavioral health standpoint, this matters: habit research consistently shows that simplifying decision points and reducing friction around food preparation is one of the most reliable levers for dietary adherence. His audience is enthusiastic enough that many pre-ordered his cookbook sight unseen — a strong signal that the community is hungry for practical frameworks, not just another steak recipe.

featured_videos.title: 1000 People Revealed Their Carnivore Struggle—It Wasn't What I Expected
featured_videos.creator: The Carnivore Pensioner
featured_videos.commentary: At 3,357 views and an 11.6% engagement rate — nearly double the dataset average — this video is punching way above its weight class. The Carnivore Pensioner surveyed 1,000 people and the result surprised even experienced practitioners: the biggest carnivore struggle isn't the food, the cravings, or the social friction — it's the isolation of doing something the mainstream thinks is insane. With 110 comments on just 3,357 views, this is one of the most comment-dense videos in this week's dataset, which tells you the audience isn't just watching — they're venting, validating, and finding their tribe.

featured_videos.title: HbA1c on Keto - What You Need to Know
featured_videos.creator: Amy Berger - Keto Without the Crazy
featured_videos.editorial_title: Your HbA1c Is High on Keto — Here's Why That's OK
featured_videos.commentary: This is one of the most important and most misunderstood lab findings in the low-carb world, and Amy Berger breaks it down with the clarity it deserves. HbA1c measures the percentage of hemoglobin that has glucose attached to it over roughly 90 days — but on a very low carbohydrate diet, red blood cells live longer because they're exposed to less oxidative stress from glucose, which means older cells accumulate more glycation even when blood glucose itself is well-controlled. A 5-year strict carnivore practitioner at 71 years old with 11% body fat and perfect CGM curves can still show an A1c of 6.1 that would alarm a conventional GP. The practical takeaway: pair your A1c with fasting glucose and a CGM before making any dietary changes based on that number alone.
